items.reason: Detail Status menus use the same container and entries as row-list menus.
`y` opens the container's Copy menu without copying.
`m` opens the container's Mute menu.
Both views use the same `I` dispatch function.
The peek's direct copy handlers are removed.
Neither detail list handles `p` directly.
Item, artifact and peek run-menu handlers remain unchanged.
An active detail flash hides the new status refusal stored in the dashboard flash.
An active detail flash also hides new copy and mute refusals.
The BROKEN detail returns before rendering the menu block, leaving opened menus invisible.
Detail menus use the existing navigation and verb dispatch handlers.
Escape clears the menu and keeps the detail open.
Detail openers bypass Selection and create singular menus.
Search narrows both detail lists; Enter applies it and restores detail controls.
Search uses case-insensitive substring terms AND-ed across id, title and type.
Item search fields exclude status.
Artifact search uses the same grammar over name and type.
Escape discards the buffer and restores the applied term.
Search opens with an empty buffer; applying it clears the query.
Printable keys reach the text field instead of detail actions.
Refresh uses the active query, and the detail header shows the applied term.
Empty search results name the query and explain how to clear it.
Artifact availability depends on the full list, so filtering preserves the view switch.
Detail search state is separate and is discarded when the detail closes.
Detail hints name the required menus and search; peek hints remove direct copy keys.
Search typing hints name only apply, cancel and help.
Help lists the required menus, container verb, search and conditional clear-search entry.
Menu and detail-search modes have separate help handling.

scores.rationale: Shared handlers and focused tests support maintainability, but flash precedence and BROKEN detail rendering leave visible failures.
